# reader-core

**Copied from the desktop app. Do not edit here.**

These files are the reading engine shared with
[TextReadsFast](https://github.com/Ramonvdo/textreadsfast) — the pivot maths that
decides which letter of a word the eye should land on, and the alignment that
puts it at a fixed screen position.

They live in both repositories because the two ship separately. That means they
can drift, and drift here is not a cosmetic problem: if the two disagree about
where the pivot goes, the same word reads differently in the app than in the
browser, and the technique depends on that position being exactly consistent.

`scripts/check-drift.mjs` compares this directory against a desktop checkout and
fails on any difference. It cannot prevent divergence — only make it visible.
Run it before releasing:

```bash
node scripts/check-drift.mjs --desktop ../textreadsfast
```

## What is here, and what deliberately is not

| File | Origin | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `orp.ts` | `src/reader/orp.ts` | Verbatim |
| `pivotOffset.ts` | `src/reader/pivotOffset.ts` | Verbatim |
| `words.ts` | part of `src/reader/tokenize.ts` | `classify` + the filler list |
| `fonts.ts` | `src/reader/fonts.ts` | One line differs — see the file |
| `fonts.css` | `src/styles/fonts.css` | Generated by the desktop's `scripts/fetch-fonts.py` |

Not copied, because this reader does not need them:

- **`StreamTokenizer`** holds back sub-word fragments that a live decoder
  commits mid-word. Captions arrive as whole phrases.
- **`cadence.ts`** paces against queue depth because live transcription cannot
  say when a word was spoken. YouTube ships timings, so pacing is a lookup.
- **`useReader.ts`** consumes Tauri events.

Changing a file here means changing it in the desktop repo too. If you find
yourself wanting to, consider whether the change belongs in `src/content/`
instead — that is this extension's own code and is free to diverge.
